svg.text: bm25.py: field-weighted BM25, end to end
Three independent BM25 indexes (title, brand, bullets). All BM25 math happens once at build time; a query is just a column-slice + sum.
① BUILD, once on first search(): get_bm25() → FieldBM25(df) → FieldIndex(texts) × 3 fields
plural -s stripped: shoes → shoe, laces → lace
real BM25 values for this tiny 3-product corpus
Per-cell BM25 weight: computed once, vectorized over every stored (product, word) cell
w = idf × tf·(K1+1) / ( tf + K1·(1 − B + B·dl/avgdl) ) idf = log(1 + (n − df + 0.5) / (df + 0.5))
K1 = 1.2, B = 0.75. The `rows` array (np.repeat over indptr) maps each stored cell back to its product so its dl can be looked up.
idf: rare words weigh more (nike 1.02 > running 0.49)
length norm (B): longer field, less per match: 0.43 < 0.49
② QUERY: search(query, k) → FieldBM25.field_scores() → rank()
→ computed, but weight 0 (tuned off, see ③)
• cols = vocab ids of query words that exist in this field. Unknown words are skipped; if none match, the field returns all zeros.
• ~1 ms/query: nothing BM25-related is recomputed. rank_bm25 would loop over all 36,984 products for every query word.
• search() uses the module-level WEIGHTS. rank() is split from field_scores() so tuning can reuse cached per-field scores.

g.text: seeded shuffle of 300 queries → 150 dev / 150 test
tune(): cache field_scores per dev query
BM25 runs once per query; only the weights change in the loop
rank top 10 → mean nDCG@10 via eval._ndcg (no log spam)

svg.text: Dev nDCG@10 for each weight combo (title fixed at 1.0)
Flat ridge at brand ≤ 0.5, bullets 0 (0.4455 – 0.4468): differences are noise on 150 queries.
Bullets add matches without precision. Heavy brand double-counts brand words already in titles.
